name: Glasgow Cathedral
description: A medieval Gothic cathedral that came through the Reformation with its roof intact. The lower church holds the tomb of St Mungo.

name: George Square
description: Glasgow’s main civic square, laid out in the late 18th century and lined with statues, with the City Chambers along its east side.

name: Glasgow School of Art
places: Glasgow School of Art, Mackintosh Building
description: The art school whose main building, designed by Charles Rennie Mackintosh, was gutted by fires in 2014 and 2018 and awaits rebuilding.

name: Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum
description: A red sandstone museum opened in 1901, with Scottish and European painting, natural history, and arms and armour. Entry is free.

name: University of Glasgow
description: Scotland’s second-oldest university, founded in 1451. Its Gothic Revival main building on Gilmorehill has a tall tower and cloisters.

name: Barrowland Ballroom
description: A dance hall in the East End above the Barras market, now a concert venue known for its sprung floor and neon sign.

name: Celtic Park
description: Celtic FC’s stadium in the East End, the largest club ground in Scotland, with room for about 60,000 fans.

name: Willow Tea Rooms
places: Mackintosh at the Willow, Sauchiehall Street
Willow Tea Rooms building, Sauchiehall Street
description: Tea rooms on Sauchiehall Street designed by Charles Rennie Mackintosh in 1903, restored and reopened in 2018 as Mackintosh at the Willow.

name: Gallery of Modern Art
places: Gallery of Modern Art, Royal Exchange Square
Duke of Wellington statue, Royal Exchange Square
description: A modern art gallery in a former merchant’s mansion. The statue of the Duke of Wellington outside usually wears a traffic cone.

name: Mary Barbour statue
description: A statue at Govan Cross of Mary Barbour, who led the 1915 rent strikes against Glasgow’s landlords. It was unveiled in 2018.
